listenings.text: People always ask me how I make my tutorials look so simple, so here is my process. First, I decide the result before I touch a single brush, because if I do not know where I am going, the video wanders. Then I do the whole look once, off camera, and I write down every step on a card. Only after that do I start filming. I say what I am doing before I do it, not after, because viewers want to know why a step matters. And I do not do everything myself. I have my lighting set up by a friend who studied film, and I get my videos edited by someone else, because editing is where I used to lose a whole weekend. The best tutorial is not the one with the most steps. It is the one where every step has a reason.

Hi, this is a message for incoming exchange students about the documents we need before registration. Please follow the steps in this order, because we cannot accept them any other way. First, request your official transcript from your home university. If it is not in English, you will need to have it translated by a certified translator. A simple translation made by a friend or an app will not be accepted. Once you have the translation, get the signed letter from your home coordinator notarized. Then send all three documents together in a single email. Do not send them one by one. Registration opens on the second Monday of the semester, and students whose documents are incomplete by then will have to register late, which means fewer electives to choose from.
